Airbags are not all bad or all good. It really depends on the accident. In some cases they can help prevent injuries, but if someone is unfortunate enough to have their arms or hands in the wrong place during an impact or (God forbid) have some type of dense object between themselves and the airbag when it's deployed, it can make things worse. IMO the are just an expensive part that needs to be replaced after an accident, and don't really make that much of a difference. The bottom line is you should ALWAYS FUCKING WEAR YOUR SEATBELT. The airbag is a supplemental safety device, it's meant to work in concert with the seatbelt and other safety features. On it's own it does very little. Modern cars are very very safe in comparison to the old days. The cars themselves are designed to crumble and absorb the impact, decreasing the force experienced by the occupant, instead of transferring it to them. They teach you in the EMS academy that there are 5 collisions in every MVA (motor vehicle accident)... The car hitting something, the person hitting the inside parts of their car, the internal organs of that person hitting their own skeletal structure, and the two rebound impacts, the person again hitting the inside of the car on the way back and their internal organs again hitting their skeletal structure. In a rollover however there can be dozens or hundreds on impacts. Nowadays, the term 'airbag' could mean so many things, because there are anywhere from 4 to 18 airbags depending on the car, each with their own sensors and conditions for triggering. I am not anti-airbag, but there is a definite lack of education of consumers when it comes to the risk versus benefits.
